findings.title: `ANY(${array})` with Prisma.sql renders invalid SQL — org/team scope queries will throw at runtime
findings.body: In `buildOrgAuthorizationCondition` (line 164 and 168) and `buildTeamAuthorizationCondition` (line 201) the code writes e.g. `Prisma.sql`("teamId" = ANY(${teamIds}))``. Prisma's tagged-template helper expands an interpolated JavaScript array into a comma-separated list of bound parameters — it does NOT serialize it as a single Postgres array parameter. So with `teamIds = [10, 20, 30]` the emitted SQL is `"teamId" = ANY($1, $2, $3)`, which Postgres rejects with `syntax error at or near "$2"` (ANY requires a single array expression or subquery). Every org-scope and team-scope query will therefore fail with a raw-query error at runtime; only the user-scope path (which has no ANY) is valid. The correct pattern is `"teamId" IN (${Prisma.join(teamIds)})` or passing a single array parameter with an explicit cast. The tests don't catch this because they only structurally compare Sql objects built with the same broken pattern.

findings.title: Public `findMany` method removed without updating callers
findings.body: The previous implementation exposed a public `findMany(findManyArgs)` method that combined authorization/filter conditions into a `bookingTimeStatusDenormalized.findMany` call. This PR deletes that method entirely and replaces it with `getBaseConditions(): Promise<Prisma.Sql>`, shifting query execution to callers via `$queryRaw`. No caller is updated in this PR (only the service and its test are changed), so any existing consumer that invokes `insightsBookingService.findMany(...)` — e.g. the insights tRPC procedures that fetch booking events/status/hourly data — will fail TypeScript compilation and lose functionality. Either keep a compatible `findMany` wrapper or update all callers in the same change.

findings.title: Integration tests never execute the generated SQL for org/team scopes
findings.body: The org-scope (line 332) and team-scope (line 295) tests assert conditions via `expect(conditions).toEqual(Prisma.sql`...`)`, which only deep-compares the Sql object's internal `strings`/`values` arrays — it never runs the SQL against the database. The only test that actually executes a query (`getBaseConditions`, line 481) uses scope `"user"`, the one code path that contains no `ANY(...)` array interpolation. As a result the tests pass while the org/team SQL is syntactically invalid (Prisma expands `ANY(${ids})` into `ANY($1, $2, ...)`, a Postgres syntax error). At least one test per scope should execute the produced conditions with `$queryRaw` against the real database so invalid generated SQL is caught.

findings.title: Org-scope expectation depends on nondeterministic row ordering for userIds
findings.body: The org-scope test asserts exact equality with `Prisma.sql`... ("userId" = ANY(${[user.id, user2.id, user3.id]})) ...`. The service builds that array from `MembershipRepository.findAllByTeamIds`, a `findMany` with no `orderBy`, so Postgres does not guarantee the row order (the user also has two memberships — team and org — that get deduped via `Set`, preserving whatever order rows came back in). If the membership rows are returned in a different order, the Sql `values` array order differs and the deep-equality assertion fails spuriously. The assertion should compare order-insensitively or the repository query should impose a deterministic order.
